# Longest Subsequence With Limited Sum.

@example Tasks of 1 and 2 minutes fit in 5; all four take exactly 12; the 1-minute task alone fits in 1.
[6,1,3,2]
[5,12,1]
=> [2,4,1]

@example No task fits in 6; both fit in 16 exactly, and in 20.
[7,9]
[6,16,20]
=> [0,2,2]

@example Three tasks of 4 minutes are three tasks: two fit in 11, and all three in 12.
[4,4,4]
[11,12]
=> [2,3]

# A single task and a single budget equal to it.
[1]
[1]
=> [1]

# A single task longer than the budget.
[5]
[4]
=> [0]

# Budgets equal to the totals of the 1 to 4 shortest tasks (1, 3, 8, 16),
# and one less than each.
[5,2,8,1]
[3,2,8,7,16,15]
=> [2,1,3,2,4,3]

# Every budget is shorter than the shortest task.
[3,4]
[1,2]
=> [0,0]

# Budgets at or above the total of all tasks.
[1,2,3]
[6,1000000]
=> [3,3]

# A long task comes first: taking tasks in list order while they fit, or
# only tasks next to each other, gives too few.
[4,1,6,1,1]
[3,4]
=> [3,3]

# Equal tasks count separately, and a repeated budget gets its answer
# each time.
[2,2,2,5]
[6,6,4,5]
=> [3,3,2,2]

# Budgets in no particular order.
[10,20,30]
[60,10,35,29,5]
=> [3,1,2,1,0]

# Values at the bounds.
[1000000,1000000,999999]
[1000000,999999,999998,1]
=> [1,1,0,0]
